# SelectorBar

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/SelectorBar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/SelectorBar.hpp`.

A row of text segments, each with an optional icon. Exactly one is selected, marked by an accent pill under its text.

The items own no content, so the app switches what is shown below in [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed). A press on an item selects it, and with focus, Left/Right move the selection. The whole strip is one tab stop. The declarative form is [ui::SelectorBar](#uiselectorbar).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* bar   = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::SelectorBarControl>(
    std::vector<ui::SelectorBarItem>{"Recent", "Shared", "Favorites"}));
auto* shown = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Recent files"));
bar->on_selection_changed([bar, shown](std::size_t) { shown->set_text(bar->selected_text() + " files"); });
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

## `ui::SelectorBar`

A horizontal segmented selector. Builds a [ui::SelectorBarControl](#uiselectorbarcontrol).

Typically paired with a [ui::Match](content-host.md#uimatch) that shows the page for the selected segment.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::size_t> tab{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .content = {
        ui::SelectorBar{
            .items          = {{"Recent", ui::Symbol::Clock}, "Shared", {"Favorites", ui::Symbol::Favorite}},
            .selected_index = tab,
        },
        ui::Match<std::size_t>{
            .value   = tab,
            .content = [](const std::size_t& i) -> ui::Spec
            { return ui::Text{.text = std::format("Page {}", i + 1)}; },
        },
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::SelectorBar{
    .items, .selected_index, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .enabled, .accessibility, .on_selection_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited,
    .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-items"></span>`items` | `ui::Binding<std::vector<ui::SelectorBarItem>>` |  | The segments, left to right: text, each with an optional icon. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-selected_index"></span>`selected_index` | `ui::TwoWayField<std::size_t>` | `{0}` | The selected segment; clamped into the item range. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_selection_changed"></span>`on_selection_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(std::size_t)>` |  | Fires with the new index when a click or the arrow keys change the selection. A bound write doesn't run it. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uiselectorbar-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::SelectorBar>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

## `ui::SelectorBarControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ValueProvider`.

A row of text segments, each with an optional icon. Exactly one is selected, marked by an accent pill under its text.

The items own no content, so the app switches what is shown below in [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed). A press on an item selects it, and with focus, Left/Right move the selection. The whole strip is one tab stop. The declarative form is [ui::SelectorBar](#uiselectorbar).

Example: 
```cpp
auto  panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* bar   = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::SelectorBarControl>(
    std::vector<ui::SelectorBarItem>{"Recent", "Shared", "Favorites"}));
auto* shown = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Recent files"));
bar->on_selection_changed([bar, shown](std::size_t) { shown->set_text(bar->selected_text() + " files"); });
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### SelectorBarControl

```cpp
SelectorBarControl() = default
```

An empty strip: nothing drawn, not focusable.

### SelectorBarControl

```cpp

```

A strip of [`items`](#items), [`selected_index`](#selected_index) selected (clamped). Raises nothing.

### items

```cpp
const std::vector<SelectorBarItem>& items() const
```

The items, in order.

### set_items

```cpp
void set_items(std::vector<SelectorBarItem> items)
```

Replaces the item list and resets the selection to index 0 without raising [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed). Updates the layout.

### selected_index

```cpp
std::size_t selected_index() const
```

The selected item's index; 0 while the list is empty.

### set_selected_index

```cpp
void set_selected_index(std::size_t index)
```

Selects the item at `index`, clamped to the item list. Does nothing, and fires nothing, if the item is already selected or the list is empty.

### selected_text

```cpp
const std::string& selected_text() const
```

The currently selected item's text, or an empty string if there are no items.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(std::size_t)> handler)
```

Fired whenever the selection changes: an item click, the arrow keys or [set_selected_index()](#set_selected_index). A call that lands on the already selected item does not fire it.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the strip holds keyboard focus.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Not a tab stop with fewer than two items, since there is nothing to switch.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

AutomationRole::Tab. The items have no content of their own, so the strip exposes the selected item's text as a read-only value.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

A single row sized to fit each item's own text, without stretching to fill the strip, plus room for the pill at the bottom of every item.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Each item's icon and text, the selected one's pill, and the focus ring while focused.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Hover tracking, and a press on an item selects it.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the selection pill's grow-in.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

ArrowLeft/ArrowRight select the previous/next item while focused (no wrap-around).

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md) as focus moves; redraws.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp

```

A square ring, a little tighter around the strip than the usual focus ring.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme&) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

## struct SelectorBarItem

One segment of a [SelectorBar](#uiselectorbar): its text and an optional icon before it.

Converts from a string, so a list of plain strings needs no item type spelled out: `.items = {"Recent", "Shared"}`, or with icons `.items = {{"Recent", ui::Symbol::Clock}, {"Shared", ui::Symbol::Share}}`.

### text

```cpp
std::string text
```

The segment's text.

### icon

```cpp
IconSource icon
```

Drawn before the text at 0.8 of a 20-DIP symbol; empty draws none.

### SelectorBarItem

```cpp
SelectorBarItem(std::string item_text, IconSource icon = {})
```

A segment showing `item_text`, with [`icon`](#icon) before it (empty: none).

### SelectorBarItem

```cpp
SelectorBarItem(const char* item_text)
```

A segment showing `item_text`.
